content:
marta: Quick RFC follow-up — proposal to split the observability ingestion path into a thin ingress/facade + domain-specific streamer workers. Goal: scale independently, reduce blast radius, and give product teams ownership.

kevin: +1 on ownership. can you call out the expected QPS and burst patterns per domain? that drives the infra sizing.

marta: current peak: ~18k events/s total, ~60% logs, 25% metrics, 15% traces. bursts from ingestion agents can be 4x for ~30s during job churn. plan is to keep the facade as a stateless HTTP/gRPC layer and move throttling/validation there.

sarah: worried about ordering and dedupe for logs — facade loses the ability to coordinate dedupe across streams. how do streamers handle idempotency?

marta: streamers will own a short-lived watermark + idempotency cache (LRU with TTL) per partition. long-term dedupe stays in storage tier. facade emits an ack-token for quick client acks if needed.

alex: what about schema evolution and transformations (redaction, normalize)? do we do that in facade or streamers?

marta: light validation + routing in facade. heavy transforms and enrichment in streamers to keep facade cheap and low-latency. transforms can be rolled out per-streamer without impacting other domains.

kevin: rollout plan idea: start with metrics streamer extract first (least downstream coupling), run in canary mode for 2 weeks. then logs, then traces. add a read-path fallback to old pipeline for 1 month.

sarah: failure modes: facade down => backpressure client-side. streamer down => buffered in Kafka for X minutes. is Kafka ops part of this RFC?

marta: Kafka retention set to 6h for hot paths, 48h for critical flows during migration. infra team will own broker scaling; streamers own consumer groups and rebalancing logic.

infra-bot: FYI: created infra ticket INFRA-907 to audit current topic partitions and retention. link: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INFRA-907 :robot_face:

alex: security: need to ensure facade enforces per-tenant quotas and PII redaction policy before any async handoff. can't rely on downstream teams for that.

marta: agreed — facade will enforce auth, per-tenant rate limits, and schema-level PII flags. redaction itself lives in streamers (configurable transforms), with a strict default policy.

kevin: sample config snippet for facade routing (pseudo):
```
routes:
  - path: /ingest/metrics
    to: metrics-streamer-topic
    qps_limit: 20000
  - path: /ingest/logs
    to: logs-streamer-topic
    qps_limit: 40000
```

sarah: monitoring + alerts: we need SLOs on facade latency (<50ms p95) and streamer consumer lag (<1k messages) during normal load. add end-to-end trace for sampling.

marta: adding SLOs to the RFC. also propose a migration checklist:
- deploy facade in front of existing pipeline in read-only (shadow) mode
- enable metrics streamer in canary, mirror traffic
- compare outputs (checksum + sample diffs)
- cutover with 10% traffic -> 50% -> 100% with rollback hooks
- monitor for data loss for 48h post-cutover

kevin: who owns the migration checklist execution?

marta: infra + observability team co-own. I'll be the tech lead for the cutover and will coordinate.

alex: one more tradeoff: adding per-streamer state (idempotency caches) increases memory footprint. alternative is central dedupe service — simpler semantics but single point of failure.

sarah: central dedupe risks SLA; prefer decentralized caches with consistent eviction and instrumentation.

marta: agreed; we'll prototype decentralized cache with metrics exported to the console and a fallback central service if needed later.

kevin: fine, looks actionable. @marta please update the RFC with the SLOs, migration checklist, and partition/retention targets. we'll discuss in the architecture sync on Thursday.

marta: will do. thanks everyone. :rocket:
